summary: The privacy flag the admin lane found is real, and the correct repair is deliberately incomplete: `profiles.show_phone` is the canonical publication gate but three separate settings writers disagree about whether they own it, and unifying them is a product/privacy decision whose two directions have opposite consequences. general-user refused to guess. Separately, `app/api/connect/sessions/route.ts` reads a phone under that gate and belongs to no agent's grant.

completed: Established that profiles.show_phone is real: created by an ACTIVE migration, present in all three generated-contract blocks, default false. It is not drift.

Established that profiles.phone does not exist in the active chain or the contract, so every `show_phone === true ? profile.phone : null` was green and returned null. Three such sites existed in the general-user grant.

Repointed the self-only preview (app/api/profile/custom-design/route.ts) to the canonical profiles.profile_data.phone with the gate expression byte-identical. The value returned is the authenticated caller's own contact data; no other subject is affected.

Pinned the LLM-prompt snapshot (lib/profile/custom-profile-prompt.ts) to `phone: null` with an explicit comment, because that value is serialized into a third-party model prompt. Repointing it would be a privacy widening disguised as a drift fix.

Added a NO-WIDENING GUARD rather than a convention: __tests__/profile/profile-contact-privacy.test.ts asserts app/api/profile/update/route.ts contains no `profileUpdate.show_phone` and no `profileUpdate.phone`, so no new writer of the gate can appear without failing a test.

Reached the same conclusion by a second, independent route: app/api/settings/route.ts accepted a caller-supplied profile_id on both verbs. RLS blocked the cross-user WRITE (profiles_update USING (id = auth.uid())) but the route still answered success:true for a zero-row update, and RLS never blocked the cross-user READ because profiles_select is USING (true) — GET returned another user's entire profile row, metadata and profile_data included, to any authenticated caller. Both verbs now return 403 and issue no query.
Did NOT add a top-level show_phone write to any route that lacked one, did NOT unify metadata.show_phone with the column, and did NOT relax any gate.
next_steps: orchestrator/product: decide ONE of two directions for the writer divergence, with the privacy consequence stated in the ticket. (A) Treat the column as canonical — then app/api/profile/update and app/api/profile/update-optimized gain the ability to publish a phone, which is a WIDENING from three writers to three writers but from the currently-effective single writer; it must ship with a consent re-prompt because existing accounts may have `metadata.show_phone: true` recorded against a gate that was never consulted. (B) Treat metadata.show_phone as canonical — then the public phone switch is permanently off, the toggle in components/settings must be removed or relabelled, and lib/profile/general-public-profile.ts:27 should keep stripping unconditionally. Option B is strictly no more permissive and is the safe default if no decision is reached.

orchestrator: assign an owner for app/api/connect/**. `app/api/connect/sessions/route.ts:146` is `Boolean(profile.show_phone && connectSettings.sharePhoneOnConnect && profile.profile_data?.phone)` — a live third-party phone surface built on the gate, and it is in no agent's grant and no manifest entry. It is NOT in the strict-ownership list of the general-user Wave 35 brief, so it was read and not edited.
Once a direction is chosen, add the corresponding assertion to __tests__/profile/profile-contact-privacy.test.ts so the decision is pinned rather than only documented.

QA-003: a phone-sharing journey cannot be certified until the direction is chosen. Today the observable behaviour is: toggling the switch in the optimized/enhanced profile settings forms changes metadata only, and the public /api/profile/<username> payload still omits phone.
blockers: The direction decision is a product/privacy call, not a schema-mechanical one. general-user cannot make it without a stated consent consequence for existing accounts.
app/api/connect/** has no owning agent, so the only other live reader of the gate cannot be fixed or verified by its owner.

No hosted evidence. profiles_select USING (true) and profiles_update USING (id = auth.uid()) were read from the active migration chain; the deployed policy set was not queried. No staging target exists.
